p:cNvPr.descr: An image depicting the three stages of respiration in the catabolism of proteins, fats, and carbohydrates. In stage 1 (acetyl-CoA production), amino and fatty acids have a blue arrow pointing down and right to a tan box with acetyl-CoA. Glucose points down with a blue arrow to pyruvate. To the right of the arrow is a blue box with glycolysis. Pyruvate points down to the acetyl-CoA box, but also has an arrow that darts off to the right pointing to CO2. This is the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex. Thin red wavy arrows, identified as e-, run down and left from the blue arrows. The arrows continue across the blue arrows of the amino and fatty acids, and extend down into the next stage. From the tan acetyl-CoA box in stage one, blue arrows extends down into stage 2 (acetyl-CoA oxidation) and form a circle for the citric acid cyle, and go right to citrate, which curves down and points to CO2, then contines to another CO2. In between, there is a thin red arrows pointing to e-. The blue arrow continues up and around to oxaloacetate. Between the second CO2 and oxyaloacetate are three thin red arrows, all pointing to e-. A thin red arrow also points down from the last stage 1 e- down to a tan box with NADH, FADH2 (reduced e- carriers). All e-s in this stage also point to the same box. A think red arrow extends from the tan box, marked as e-, and points to a blue box in the third stage (which is electron transfer and oxidative phosphorylation). The blue box is the respiratory (electron-transfer) chain. To the right of the box, 2H+ plus 1/2O2 points down to H20 with a curved blue arrow. The arc of the arrow touches the blue box. Below the blue box is another curved blue arrow, with ADP + Pi pointing right to ATP in a light orange oval. The arc of this curved arrow touches the blue box.
